title: Customer legal briefing and incident timeline
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact customer-facing legal & timeline briefing for incidents where customers may request regulatory evidence, replay consent, or contractual remediation. Designed for CS leads + legal to adapt and send to impacted tenants. Not final legal language — use as the operational briefing and attach final counsel-approved statements when required.

Quick elevator (what to send within 60 minutes):
- 1–2 sentence plain-language summary of what happened and current service state.
- Scope statement: which API surfaces, regions, and tenant identifiers (by consent) were affected.
- Actions we took and immediate mitigations.
- Next steps and customer choices (replay opt-in, evidence package, SLA credit request).
- Contact + escalation path.

Incident summary (example language to adapt):
- Incident id: INC-8742 (internal)
- Short summary: Between 2029-03-03 22:14 UTC and 2029-03-03 23:07 UTC a routing configuration change caused inference requests in eu-west-1 to be routed to a mixed-quantization model variant that produced degraded outputs for a subset of tenant workloads. We detected increased error rates and degraded ranking stability; serving latency also spiked during remediation.
- Current status (as of 2029-03-05 09:00 UTC): service restored to normal across all regions; a targeted rollback and routing safeguards are in place.

Technical timeline (UTC) - include timestamps you can verify:
- 2029-03-03 22:09: change staged in canary (automated rollout started).
- 2029-03-03 22:14: rollout crossed threshold and new routing profile applied to 12% of traffic in eu-west-1.
- 2029-03-03 22:22: telemetry alarm: ranking stability metric exceeded threshold. Ops on-call alerted via PagerDuty.
- 2029-03-03 22:30: triage: identified routing policy mismatch (quantized variant selected for low-seq requests).
- 2029-03-03 22:45: rollback initiated for canary.
- 2029-03-03 22:57: rollback completed; routing reverted.
- 2029-03-03 23:07: post-rollout checks passing; system marked degraded->recovering.
- 2029-03-04 02:40: extended verification and targeted trace collection finished.
- 2029-03-05 08:50: final status confirmation and customer communication plan drafted.

Impact scope (how to describe):
- Who was affected: a subset of tenant requests routed through eu-west-1 during the window above; impact varied by prompt pattern (shorter context and heavy ranking workloads experienced more instability).
- What was observed: increased refusal/partial outputs, ranking regressions, and elevated latency. No confirmed data exfiltration.
- Data: we observed no unauthorized data access; logs and traces show normal ACLs.

Customer-facing remediation options (present as choices):
1) Evidence package (automatic): we will assemble a time-bound evidence package with request ids, timestamps, routing decisions, and sample request/response artifacts for verification. This package will contain hashed tenant ids; raw request content is included only if tenant opts in.
2) Replay & verification (opt-in): customers can opt-in to a controlled replay of affected requests to compare outputs on the corrected routes. Replays are conducted in a sandbox with customer consent; we provide a diff and verifier checklist.
3) SLA credit request: eligible customers may open a request for SLA review. We will include impact windows and per-tenant metrics for evaluation.
4) Legal/regulatory packet: for customers with compliance needs (SOC2/ISO/FINRA/PDPA), we will assemble a tailored packet including timeline, mitigations, and operator logs. This is available upon request and may require a DPA amendment for deeper artifacts.

How to collect customer choices (proposed template):
- Reply to this message with one or more of the following options: 
  A) Send me the evidence package (automatic redaction).
  B) I authorize a controlled replay of my requests — contact me for scheduling.
  C) Submit SLA credit for my account.
  D) I require a compliance packet — legal contact: <customer-legal@example.com>.
- Include preferred contact and a primary point-of-contact for further questions.

Recommended internal playbook actions for CS + Legal (checklist):
- [ ] Verify tenant list and affected request ids from ops trace export (owner: ops).
- [ ] Prepare evidence package (owner: CS lead).
- [ ] Draft replay schedule and sandbox parameters (owner: SE + customer).
- [ ] Coordinate with Legal to prepare compliance packet and any DPA language (owner: Legal).
- [ ] Open SLA review case if customer requests (owner: CS ops).
- [ ] Confirm no PII breach; if observed escalate to Security and Legal immediately.

Suggested phrasing for public status page update (short):
- "We experienced a routing configuration regression affecting model variant selection in eu-west-1 on 2029-03-03. Service has been restored; we are offering evidence and replay options to impacted customers and will publish a post-incident summary once root cause verification is complete."

Suggested phrasing for tenant direct email (longer):
- Lead: quick plain-language summary.
- Middle: what we know, why it happened at a high level (configuration rollout mismatch), what we changed, why outputs may have differed for you.
- Choices: enumerate Evidence / Replay / SLA / Compliance packet.
- Closing: contact, timeline for full postmortem (target: 14 days), link to internal ticket.

Draft postmortem excerpt for customers (to be expanded into final):
- Root cause: rollout gating did not account for quantization compatibility checks for short-sequence ranking workloads; as a result, a quantized model variant with lower ranking stability was selected for a portion of traffic. Corrective action: rollout service now enforces model-compatibility gating and added pre-rollout simulation on representative sample prompts.
- Preventive controls: stronger canary thresholds, simulation suite for quantization/compatibility, and a new alert for ranking-skew anomalies.

Privacy & data handling notes to include: 
- Evidence packages will default to hashed identifiers; raw payloads are shared only with explicit tenant consent.
- Any replay executed will run in an isolated sandbox and will not alter production logs.
- Retention: evidence/replay artifacts generated for this incident will be retained for 90 days unless the customer requests earlier deletion.

Operational contact list for customers:
- Primary CS lead: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai)
- Ops on-call escalation: Diego Moreno (pager contact included in ticket)
- Legal intake: legal-ops@redwood.ai (for compliance packet requests)

Attachment checklist when sending to customer:
- Incident timeline (simple CSV with timestamps)
- Evidence package (if requested) or offer link to request it
- Replay consent form (short) if customer wants replay
- SLA credit request form link

Open questions / items for legal before final send:
- Does the compliance packet need a non-disclosure addendum for raw payloads?
- Is the proposed 90-day retention appropriate for regulated customers?
- Do we need a special channel for EU data subject requests tied to this incident?

Notes to CS drafting the message (voice + tone):
- Keep it plain, avoid technical jargon in the first paragraph.
- Lead with remediation and choices — customers want to know what they can do.
- When in doubt, offer replay + evidence rather than insisting on telemetry-only explanations.

References & artifacts to attach internally:
- Confluence incident draft: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-8742
- Ops runbook used: JIRA-OPS-1456
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/INC-8742

Versioning and follow-up cadence:
- Initial note: within 60–90 minutes of visible impact containment.
- Evidence package: preparatory draft within 48 hours.
- Postmortem (customer-facing): target 14 days; interim update at 72 hours if investigation extends.

Free-form notes / scratchpad (internal):
- Customers that have strict ranking workloads (search, summarization with short cores) should be prioritized for proactive outreach.
- Consider an automated tenant signal that offers evidence/replay links from the status page for impacted tenants by id.
- Flag any requests that may need redaction review before release.

-- end of briefing --

(Use this doc as the operational template; legal should approve wording for compliance packet and any raw-data sharing.)
